To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ATP recovery is severely limited in areas of cat cortex that have been depleted by 30 minutes of ischemia.
(a) postischemic ATP resynthesis is severely limited, (b) NADH levels do not reflect the degree of energy depletion, and (c) ATP resynthesis may be limited by the availability of NAD.
the recovery of ATP following cerebral ischemia is impaired by a failure of NADH production.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of transient ischemia on cerebral energy metabolism.
the effects of temporary ischemia on the cerebral circulation and the energy metabolism in the cat cortex.
the mechanisms that control ATP synthesis in brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the postischemic recovery process of brain is a complicated phenomenon which is influenced by a variety of factors.
the failure to restore ATP after ischemia is due to a defect in the production of NAD+ from NADH.
the factors limiting regeneration of ATP after temporary ischemia include (a) a failure of oxidation of NADH and (b) a failure of production of NADPH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the failure of ATP resynthesis after ischemia was due to a defect in the oxidative phosphorylation system.
ATP resynthesis is limited by the availability of NADH.
ATP recovery is impaired because the production of NAD+ is limited by an inability of mitochondria to oxidize NADH.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ATP recovery after ischemia is a very slow process, even when O2 delivery is not limiting.
ATP synthesis is impaired in the post-ischemic brain, and that this impairment is due to an inability to produce NADH.
the post-ischemic recovery process is not as simple as we had originally thought.
